target_customer: Brazilian students seeking discounted college programs, paid by partner colleges through commissions on enrollments
problem: Brazilian private colleges have unfilled seats while students struggle to afford tuition and compare programs.
business_model: Marketplace taking enrollment fees from partner institutions for discounted seats
product_category: Education marketplace (Quero Bolsa) and edtech group

founders.name: Bernardo de Padua
education: Dropped out of a Master's in CS in 2010 to start a first startup
previous_startups: A first startup started in 2010, which he describes as failed (YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says he scaled the company from 0 to 800 employees, mostly bootstrapped, 2013 to 2019.

founders.name: Thiago Brandão
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: A two-sided marketplace and enrollment workflow, with the difficulty in sales operations and partner integration rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Hundreds of partner college relationships and student traffic create a modest two-sided network; the model of discounted unfilled seats is copyable, as Educa Mais Brasil shows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Quero instead acquired others: the Brazilian QuinStreet education operation in January 2020 and invested in Melhor Escola in 2019; it later merged with Allevo to form Qeevo.

market_need_then: Brazilian private colleges had idle seats and the company says its Quero Bolsa was created to fill them and widen access to higher education, according to founder statements reported in Portuguese press.

branding.name_origin: Quero is Portuguese for 'I want'; no source explains the choice.
branding.domain_note: Consumer site is querobolsa.com.br; no source on domain history.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain consumer language about price and scholarships

branding.brand_signature: Quero Bolsa, a scholarship marketplace brand

rebrands.why: Not stated; the Quero Bolsa product brand stayed unchanged (Portuguese search summary, undated).

branding.community_and_virality: Large editorial magazine on the site and a Reclame Aqui RA1000 badge listed on the company site.

brand_strength.rationale: Quero Bolsa is described as the largest scholarship service in Brazil with over 1.6 million enrolled students per the company.

outcome_analysis: Quero Education grew from a 2013 scholarship marketplace to the largest scholarship service in Brazil by its own account, scaling mostly bootstrapped to hundreds of employees by 2019 and making acquisitions such as QuinStreet Brazil in 2020. It then merged with Allevo into the Qeevo group. Strength came from filling colleges' idle seats at scale, with modest outside funding relative to its size.
notes: The Series A rests on databases only (CB Insights: $8.5M, 2018-10-24; Seedtable also lists $8.5M in 2018-10 and names Redpoint eVentures as lead, while an earlier note named Iporanga Ventures, so investors are left blank). Other single-source figures are not recorded: CB Insights total 10.22M over 9 rounds, Seedtable total 9.5M over four rounds, Portuguese Wikipedia via SeedTable about R$60M raised from Y Combinator, Endeavor, Iporanga and Omidyar Network (Contxto repeats about R$60M equity by 2018), and a startups.com.br headline saying GP Investimentos planned to convert US$5M of convertible debentures. YC's 120K for 7% is the standard deal. 500 Startups put in about US$100K per Preqin (2017-08), not recorded. The $8.5M figure is not confirmed by press in the cross-check. Direct fetch of fusoesaquisicoes returned 403. Competitor list left empty: Educa Mais Brasil appears only in undated comparison articles. YC page lists team size 200 versus the founder bio's 800 at peak. The Qeevo merger was described as planned in the source; completion not verified.
